issues.detail: Example 2 has no runnable code (only prose describing calls to obb.economy.cpi and interest_rates, joining and plotting), so only one of the two examples is a complete demonstration.

scenarios.name: agent-safe-stock-snapshot
scenarios.rationale: A meets the rubric by importing `obb`, setting explicit free providers (cboe, sec, nasdaq), using `.to_dataframe()`, and commenting on the sec versus nasdaq revenue column names and `.columns`. B relies on yfinance, which the rubric bans, and uses `.to_df()`, so it fails the core constraints.

scenarios.name: inflation-vs-rates-free-data
scenarios.rationale: Both use OECD for cpi and interest_rates and mention switching to provider="fred" with a free key, but B joins the two DataFrames and plots them, and recommends the FRED_API_KEY environment variable rather than hard-coding. A plots the series without an explicit join, and its FRED credential example hard-codes the key, which the rubric advises against, even though it mentions persisting it in the settings file.

scenarios.name: install-and-expose-mcp-for-agent
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: it gives `openbb[routers]` or individual packages, discovery with `dir(obb)` and the `provider` annotation, `openbb-mcp --transport stdio` with `--allowed-categories`, and loopback binding. B recommends `openbb[all]` and `openbb.build()` instead of `[routers]`, and it uses `help()` for discovery rather than the signature or annotation. B also guesses at flag names such as `--default-categories` and never names `--allowed-categories`, though it does state the 127.0.0.1 binding.
